question: Should an empty SQLite registry with a remaining runs.json file and no durable receipt fail safe by preserving and warning, rather than automatically importing the legacy file?
rationale: Source inspection and proof can establish transaction safety, but they cannot determine whether an unreceipted legacy file is authoritative upgrade data or stale state that would resurrect deleted runs.

options.title: Approve preserve-and-warn
options.body: Confirm the proposed fail-safe contract, land after rebasing and green checks, and treat explicit doctor recovery as the supported ambiguity path.

options.title: Add explicit resolution first
options.body: Require doctor to offer a tested import-or-retire action before merging so operators can resolve preserved sources without manual database or file work.

options.title: Retain automatic import
options.body: Reject this contract and redesign migration provenance while accepting that empty canonical state cannot distinguish authoritative legacy data from stale resurrection data.

recommendation.title: Approve preserve-and-warn
recommendation.body: Confirm the proposed fail-safe contract, land after rebasing and green checks, and treat explicit doctor recovery as the supported ambiguity path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged SQLite migration and maintenance work is the closest available ownership signal for this compatibility decision.
